# Radio group — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for a radio group when the choices are few enough to show together and only one may be chosen: a plan, a delivery speed, a severity. Showing the whole set at once is the point — if the list is long enough to need scrolling or searching, that is a select, and if the answer is really a series of independent switches, that is a checkbox group. Give the set a question with a Fieldset and legend, because the group itself has no label slot and an unlabelled set of options is a list of guesses.

### Usage

**Do**

- Use when exactly one option in a set may be chosen — grouped by shared name.
- Place the group in a `radiogroup` with a visible label.
- Give every radio an `aria-label` — radios are never auto-labelled.

**Don't**

- Don't wrap radios inside a `<label>` — it stops screen readers announcing the group count.
- Don't use for independent multi-choices — that is a checkbox.
- Don't use for a single on/off — that is a switch.

### Anatomy

| Part | Role |
| --- | --- |
| RadioGroup | The set. Owns the selected value and enforces that only one is chosen at a time. |
| RadioGroupItem | One option. Renders its own `<label>` around the control and the label text, so the name is associated without wiring. |

### FAQ

**Radio or select?**

Radio shows every option at once (2–5 visible choices). Select hides options behind a menu — better for 6+ options or tight space.

## Native

### Features

Reach for a radio group when the answer is one of a known few and the alternatives should be visible at once: a plan, a delivery method, a size. The group owns the selection and `value` is a single `string`, which is the whole difference from a checkbox group — one choice versus many, and the type says so. `disabled` on the group disables every item. Each item's `children` is required here, unlike the checkbox group's optional one, because a radio with no label is a radio nobody can tell apart from its neighbours.
